_about: Components that are present in a third-party image but never executed by the service that runs it.
Architecture only: a statement names a component and why it never runs, never a vulnerability identifier (the validator rejects one).
Each statement becomes OpenVEX not_affected statements (one per matching finding) on the runner; see scripts/triage-image-findings.py.
OpenVEX needs one vulnerability per statement and has no expiry field, so the per-component declaration and its expiry live here.

verified_against: the image references the evidence was checked on. When a pin moves, the statement holds only if its image_checks pass on the new image (automatic); a statement without image_checks needs a person to re-verify and update verified_against.
Validated by scripts/validate-vex.sh: OpenVEX justification, reason of 40+ characters, evidence, at least one compose condition, expiry within 365 days.
A statement that fails any of this is not applied: its findings come back on the code-scanning tab.

statements.reason: gosu only drops from root to the postgres user once at container start (setuid and exec); it never calls the Go standard-library packages the scanner flags, such as net/http, crypto/tls or archive/tar.
evidence: The postgres images start through docker-entrypoint.sh, whose only gosu call is `exec gosu postgres "$BASH_SOURCE" "$@"` (docker-library/postgres, docker-entrypoint.sh); pgvector/pgvector keeps that entrypoint.
gosu's SECURITY.md: CVEs in Go interfaces gosu never invokes (net/http, archive/tar, encoding/xml, ...) do not apply; govulncheck is the arbiter.
Scope is the stdlib module inside that one binary; findings in gosu's own dependencies stay on the tab.

statements.reason: The image's /entrypoint.sh starts litestream only when LITESTREAM_REPLICA_URL is set; compose does not set it, so calnode runs directly and the bundled litestream binary is never executed.
evidence: /entrypoint.sh in ghcr.io/calnode/calnode:0.14.0: `if [ -n "$LITESTREAM_REPLICA_URL" ]; then ... exec litestream replicate ...; else exec /calnode; fi`.
deploy/docker-compose.yml calnode: no LITESTREAM_REPLICA_URL in environment and no env_file (checked by the condition below).

statements.reason: The runtime only shells out to kubectl in its k8s backend; RUNTIME_BACKEND defaults to docker and compose does not set it, so bots are started through the Docker socket bridge and kubectl never runs.
evidence: vexaai/v012-runtime:v0.13.1 /app/src/runtime_kernel/__main__.py: `kind = os.getenv("RUNTIME_BACKEND", "docker")`; kubectl is called only from k8s_backend.py.
deploy/docker-compose.yml vexa12-runtime: no RUNTIME_BACKEND, Docker socket mounted from runtime-api-socket-proxy (checked by the condition below).

statements.reason: The tar copy sits inside pnpm's corepack download cache, which is only used to install packages; the image starts its harness with --start-docker, which skips the install step and starts every role with plain node, so pnpm and its tar never run.
evidence: Image config of ghcr.io/firecrawl/firecrawl:2.11.831 and 2.11.860: Entrypoint docker-entrypoint.sh (node's, which only execs its arguments), Cmd `node dist/src/harness.js --start-docker`, WorkingDir /app.

/app/dist/src/harness.js: `pnpm install` and `pnpm build` run only when the first argument is neither --start-built nor --start-docker, and with --start-docker each role is started as `node <roleEntry> <role>` instead of `pnpm <script>`.
Apart from test files under dist/src/__tests__, which the image never runs, harness.js (and its source map) is the only file under /app/dist that names pnpm or corepack.

deploy/docker-compose.yml firecrawl-api: no entrypoint or command override (checked by the condition below). The path names the cached pnpm version, so a newer cache in a later image is a new component and its findings come back.
